summary: Well-executed, fully archived paired preregistered study comparing LLM-only generation to a deterministic generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline on 200 synthetic intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Execution artifacts and analyses are consistent and complete: all 200 initial LLM candidates passed the deterministic validator; no repairs were invoked; paired table n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; exact McNemar p=1.0. The manuscript reports a null/negative confirmatory outcome and includes disclosure and artifact hashes. Key reproducibility gaps and interpretive limitations are noted but need clearer, prominent reporting and wording revisions before finalisation.
critical_issues: The preregistered confirmatory test is effectively uninformative because the baseline failure rate was 0% (baseline success 200/200). The manuscript must explicitly state in Methods and Results that the pre-registered power assumptions (baseline unsafe incidence ≈30%) were not met and that the planned hypothesis test cannot provide evidence of a ≥50% relative reduction under the observed data distribution.

The preregistered Mininet holdout-selection seed (needed to exactly reproduce which tasks were used for the emulator contamination check) is not present as a labeled artifact in the bundle. The manuscript must prominently report this missing preregistered artifact in Methods/Results and explain the reproducibility consequence (i.e., inability to deterministically re-run the exact holdout emulator checks).

The execution metadata leaves ambiguity about how deterministic generation semantics were enforced at the provider level: model_configuration.json shows "temperature": null. The manuscript must explicitly state, using the archived provider-call traces, how determinism/shared-initial semantics were implemented (e.g., adapter-enforced single shared candidate, caching, fixed-seed provider parameters) and point to the provider-call artifacts that demonstrate identical initial candidates across conditions.
required_revisions: In Methods and Results, add an explicit, prominent statement that the observed baseline failure rate was 0% and that, therefore, the preregistered confirmatory McNemar test and the preregistered power calculation were not informative for the hypothesized ≥50% relative reduction; rephrase any language implying the hypothesis was 'refuted' to instead explain that the test could not discriminate effects under the observed event rates.

In Methods (not only Discussion), disclose the missing preregistered holdout-selection seed artifact and explain the practical reproducibility implication (that the exact randomized holdout selection for Mininet cannot be deterministically reconstructed from the bundle), referencing the contamination_summary artifact which shows no disagreements.

Add a concise, evidence-backed description in Methods of how deterministic/shared-initial generation semantics were realized: cite the specific provider-call trace files and the model_configuration.json entry, and state whether determinism arose from provider parameters, adapter caching of one shared initial candidate, or other mechanism (use the archived provider_call artifacts to support the statement).
optional_revisions: Reduce provenance/hash density in the main narrative: move long lists of artifact hashes and file-level provenance into the Disclosure Statement or a compact artifact-index paragraph, and focus the main text on literature context, methods, and interpretation to improve readability.

Expand discussion of implications for operational validator completeness (examples of validator coverage gaps) and outline a prioritized experimental plan for follow-up studies (e.g., higher-temperature sampling, adversarial tasks, multi-model comparisons, multi-step repair budgets).

If space permits within the five-page limit, include one short illustrative example (before–after validator trace) showing how a repair would have been invoked in a task that fails the validator to make the GVR workflow clearer to readers; otherwise reference a single representative artifact file.
